newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - PowerGen gives buyback outlook.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - PowerGen gives buyback outlook.

text.p: British electricity generator PowerGen Plc said on Thursday it expected to start its programme to buy back up to 10 percent of its shares in coming weeks.

"We'll do it over the coming weeks, as and when the board feels it's appropriate. Clearly, we need to see a steady share price, and we need to determine when the moment is right," finance director Peter Hickson told Reuters in an interview.
"One would probably assume it's sooner rather than later, but that depends how you define sooner and later," he added.
Hickson said the company had not set a cutoff date for the buyback programme, which might be spread out over months.
PowerGen's shares were up 1.5p at 552 by 1018 but down from an intraday high of 558p after it unveiled the buyback and posted first-half results in line with analysts' expectations.
"We had a very strong performance from our UK business," Hickson said. "There was a three percent increase in electricity demand, which was very much a reflection of a buoyant economy."
PowerGen's interim pretax profits rose four percent to 138 million stg, excluding an exceptional credit of 69 million stg from the sale of its 21 percent stake in Midlands Electricity Plc .
Analysts had expected the firm to report pretax profits of 124 to 151 million stg for the six months to September 29.
PowerGen also raised its interim dividend to 7.8p from 6.5p.
The company's buyback plan came amid market speculation about its strategy after its bid for Midlands, a regional power firm, was blocked by regulators this year.

"We believe that, having reviewed our balance sheet, the share buyback offers the best deal for our shareholders," Hickson said, adding that the company was continually looking at potential projects and acquisitions.
"We have a number of things we are reviewing. There are no plans to move forward at this stage," he said.
According to its balance sheet, PowerGen spent about 346 million stg in the first-half on share buybacks.

Hickson said the company was not currently planning any acquisition on the scale of the Midlands offer, adding that it was unlikely it would bid for another of Britain's independent regional electricity companies.
"We feel that this could be another good year of progress. We're optimistic that our performance for the full year will be very acceptable," he said.
